title: Where JavaScript runs: browser and server runtimes
learningObjectives: Explain where javascript runs: browser and server runtimes and describe JavaScript's role in web development.

understand.concept: JavaScript can run in browsers and server-side runtimes such as Node.js and other compatible environments. The language is shared, but the available host APIs differ: browsers provide DOM and window-related APIs, while server runtimes provide file, process, and networking capabilities under their own security models.
understand.whyItMatters: Code that uses document or window will not run unchanged in a server runtime. Understanding the host environment prevents accidental assumptions about APIs and permissions.
understand.analogy: The language is the same toolkit, but the workbench and available tools differ between a browser and a server runtime.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; language standards and host runtime APIs have precise technical boundaries.

explain.narrative: This example depends on the browser DOM. A server-side JavaScript program would use different APIs to produce output.

examples.explanation: This example depends on the browser DOM. A server-side JavaScript program would use different APIs to produce output.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser page displays or updates text using JavaScript.

practise.guidedTask: Identify which parts of a sample script depend on the browser DOM and which use core JavaScript language features.
practise.independentTask: Create a short explanation and runnable example that separates core JavaScript language features from browser-specific APIs.
hints: Identify the runtime before using host APIs.
Use original examples and explain each line.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Where JavaScript runs: browser and server runtimes</title></head><body>
<script>const message='Browser runtime';document.body.insertAdjacentText('beforeend',message);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which API is specific to browser documents and not available by default in Node.js?
questions.explanation: document is a browser DOM API and is not a built-in global in a standard Node.js process.

questions.prompt: What should you identify before using a JavaScript API?
questions.explanation: Available APIs depend on whether code runs in a browser, server runtime, or another host.
